result: every claim tagged with a source was found in that source, and every line marked inference is a fair reading of the source it names or the document's own reasoning
notes: Reset every flop: lowRISC says sequential statements for state assignments should contain only reset values and the next-state assignment, and its resets are active-low and asynchronous by default; the document's rule that every flop holding state gets a reset value is read from that line.

No latches: lowRISC requires a default case item to avoid accidental latch inference and, without defaults before the case, every variable assigned in one item assigned in all items including the default; the document's first sentence on how a latch is inferred summarises those rules.
Proof setup: SBY gives depth a default of 20 for bmc and cover, and in prove mode it is the k-induction depth of the smtbmc engine (other engines ignore it), the engine the document uses.
The f_past_valid guard and the assumption of reset on the first cycle are in the section of the ZipCPU post on capturing the rules in formal properties.
